Project Foundations for Data Science: FoodHub Data Analysis¶

Marks: 60

Context¶

The number of restaurants in New York is increasing day by day. Lots of students and busy professionals rely on those restaurants due to their hectic lifestyles. Online food delivery service is a great option for them. It provides them with good food from their favorite restaurants. A food aggregator company FoodHub offers access to multiple restaurants through a single smartphone app.

The app allows the restaurants to receive a direct online order from a customer. The app assigns a delivery person from the company to pick up the order after it is confirmed by the restaurant. The delivery person then uses the map to reach the restaurant and waits for the food package. Once the food package is handed over to the delivery person, he/she confirms the pick-up in the app and travels to the customer's location to deliver the food. The delivery person confirms the drop-off in the app after delivering the food package to the customer. The customer can rate the order in the app. The food aggregator earns money by collecting a fixed margin of the delivery order from the restaurants.

Objective¶

The food aggregator company has stored the data of the different orders made by the registered customers in their online portal. They want to analyze the data to get a fair idea about the demand of different restaurants which will help them in enhancing their customer experience. Suppose you are hired as a Data Scientist in this company and the Data Science team has shared some of the key questions that need to be answered. Perform the data analysis to find answers to these questions that will help the company to improve the business.

Data Description¶

The data contains the different data related to a food order. The detailed data dictionary is given below.

Data Dictionary¶

  • order_id: Unique ID of the order
  • customer_id: ID of the customer who ordered the food
  • restaurant_name: Name of the restaurant
  • cuisine_type: Cuisine ordered by the customer
  • cost: Cost of the order
  • day_of_the_week: Indicates whether the order is placed on a weekday or weekend (The weekday is from Monday to Friday and the weekend is Saturday and Sunday)
  • rating: Rating given by the customer out of 5
  • food_preparation_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the restaurant to prepare the food. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the restaurant's order confirmation and the delivery person's pick-up confirmation.
  • delivery_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the delivery person to deliver the food package. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the delivery person's pick-up confirmation and drop-off information

Multivariate Analysis¶

Question 12: Perform a multivariate analysis to explore relationships between the important variables in the dataset. (It is a good idea to explore relations between numerical variables as well as relations between numerical and categorical variables) [10 marks]¶

Correlation among Numerial Variables

Correlation heatmap among all the variables

In [200]:
# Replace 'Not given' with NaN in the 'rating' column
df_numeric = df.copy()
df_numeric['rating'] = df_numeric['rating'].replace('Not given', np.nan)
# Convert the 'rating' column to numeric
df_numeric['rating'] = pd.to_numeric(df_numeric['rating'])

# Select only numerical columns for correlation analysis, excluding 'order_id' and 'customer_id'
numerical_cols = df_numeric.select_dtypes(include=np.number).columns.drop(['order_id', 'customer_id']).tolist()

# Calculate the correlation matrix
corr_matrix = df_numeric[numerical_cols].corr()

# Plotting the heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, annot=True,vmin=-1, vmax=1, cmap='coolwarm', fmt=".2f", linewidths=.5)
plt.title('Correlation Heatmap of Numerical Variables')
plt.show()

Observation:¶

Cost of the order shows very weak or no correlation with delivery time, suggesting higher-priced orders are not necessarily delivered slower.

Most numerical variables do not exhibit strong linear relationships, except for preparation time contributing to delivery time.

Data points are widely scattered, reinforcing that delivery time is influenced by multiple factors rather than a single variable.

Ratings by Day of the Week

Weekend orders show a slightly higher frequency of good ratings, aligning with faster average delivery times observed on weekends.

5-star ratings dominate on both weekday and weekend. Weekend has a slightly higher share of 5-star ratings (about 51.1% weekend vs 49.4% weekday among rated orders).

Weekdays have a higher share of 3-star ratings (≈ 18.5% weekday vs 15.2% weekend), indicating slightly worse experiences on weekdays.

Ratings vs Cuisines

Most cuisines are dominated by ratings 4 and 5, with 5 generally the most frequent.

High-volume cuisines like American, Japanese, Italian, Chinese show lots of ratings across 3/4/5 — meaning they drive most of the rating patterns overall.

Some cuisines show very high 5-star share (e.g., Spanish, Thai, Indian) but these categories have low rating counts, so they’re less reliable for strong conclusions.

No cuisine stands out as consistently extreme, though some low-sample cuisines show more visible variation.

Question 13: The company wants to provide a promotional offer in the advertisement of the restaurants. The condition to get the offer is that the restaurants must have a rating count of more than 50 and the average rating should be greater than 4. Find the restaurants fulfilling the criteria to get the promotional offer. [3 marks]¶

In [210]:
# Remove 'Not given' ratings and convert rating to numeric
df_ratings = df[df['rating'] != 'Not given'].copy()
df_ratings['rating'] = df_ratings['rating'].astype(int)

# Group by restaurant and compute count and mean rating
restaurant_stats = df_ratings.groupby('restaurant_name')['rating'].agg(
    rating_count='count',
    avg_rating='mean')

# Apply the conditions
eligible_restaurants = restaurant_stats[
    (restaurant_stats['rating_count'] > 50) &
    (restaurant_stats['avg_rating'] > 4)].sort_values(by='rating_count', ascending=False)

eligible_restaurants

Observations:¶

Four restaurants meet the promotional criteria of more than 50 ratings and an average rating above 4.

Shake Shack has the highest number of ratings (133), indicating strong customer engagement.

The Meatball Shop has the highest average rating (4.51) among eligible restaurants. All selected restaurants have consistently high average ratings (above 4.2), with substantial rating volumes.

These restaurants demonstrate both high customer satisfaction and sufficient rating volume, making them reliable and suitable candidates for the promotional offer.

# Calculate commission per order
df['company_revenue'] = np.where(
    df['cost_of_the_order'] > 20,
    df['cost_of_the_order'] * 0.25,
    np.where(
        df['cost_of_the_order'] > 5,
        df['cost_of_the_order'] * 0.15,
        0
    )
)

# Total net revenue

Conclusion and Recommendations¶

Question 17: What are your conclusions from the analysis? What recommendations would you like to share to help improve the business? (You can use cuisine type and feedback ratings to drive your business recommendations.) [6 marks]¶

Conclusions:¶

  • Restaurant demand is highly concentrated: The revenue table shows that a small number of restaurants (e.g. Shake Shack, The Meatball Shop, Blue Ribbon Sushi/Fried Chicken) contribute a disproportionately large share of total revenue, indicating strong customer preference for a limited set of restaurants.

  • American cuisine dominates demand: Countplots show American cuisine has the highest number of orders, especially on weekends, making it the most popular cuisine category on the platform.

  • Weekend orders outperform weekdays in customer experience: Boxplots and rating countplots show faster delivery times and slightly higher 5-star ratings on weekends, indicating smoother operations and better customer satisfaction during weekends.

  • Delivery time is a key driver of customer satisfaction: Ratings vs delivery time plots show that higher ratings are concentrated at lower delivery times, while longer delivery times lead to more rating variability and lower scores.

  • Food preparation time impacts delivery performance: The correlation heatmap and scatter plots show that longer food preparation time contributes to longer delivery time, even though overall correlations remain weak.

  • Order cost does not strongly influence delivery or ratings: Correlation analysis and boxplots show minimal relationship between order cost and delivery time or ratings, suggesting customers care more about speed and food quality than price.

  • Cuisine type influences ratings: Rating vs cuisine countplots show that some cuisines receive consistently higher proportions of 4 to 5 star ratings, while others have more mixed feedback, indicating differences in perceived quality or consistency.

  • High-volume cuisines drive overall platform ratings: American, Japanese, Italian, and Chinese cuisines dominate rating counts, meaning customer satisfaction trends are heavily influenced by these cuisines.

  • Delivery performance is consistent across cuisines: Delivery-time-by-cuisine boxplots show no cuisine consistently suffers extreme delays, indicating operational fairness across restaurant types.

Recommendations:¶

  • Prioritise top-performing restaurants: Strengthen partnerships with high-revenue and high-demand restaurants (e.g. Shake Shack, Blue Ribbon brands) through promotions, featured listings, or exclusive deals to retain and grow core demand.

  • Expand and promote high-demand cuisines: Increase onboarding and visibility of American, Japanese, Italian, and Chinese restaurants, as these cuisines drive most orders and ratings on the platform.

  • Target weekday delivery inefficiencies: Improve weekday delivery performance by: Increasing delivery partner availability Optimising route allocation during peak weekday hours This directly addresses slower weekday delivery times and lower ratings.

  • Use ratings to improve restaurant quality: Identify cuisines or restaurants with lower or inconsistent ratings and work with them on:

  1. Food quality consistency
  2. Preparation efficiency
  3. Packaging and order accuracy

  • Reduce food preparation delays for slower restaurants: Since preparation time impacts delivery time, collaborate with restaurants showing higher prep times to streamline kitchen workflows and order readiness.

  • Leverage weekend performance strategies: Apply weekend operational strategies (staffing, delivery allocation) to weekdays, as weekends show better delivery speed and customer satisfaction.

  • Use cuisine-based personalization: Recommend high-rated cuisines more prominently to new or repeat customers to improve overall platform satisfaction.

  • Focus on experience, not pricing: Since cost does not strongly affect ratings, the company should prioritise speed, reliability, and food quality over discounts or price-based competition.
